domain_title: Models, agents, providers, tools and supply chain
title: Shadow AI component usage
canonical_definition: Unregistered or uncontrolled models, tools, providers, prompts or agent capabilities are used.

conditions: All AI systems, including externally hosted and embedded AI components.
Record the assessed release, operating scope and evidence that supports any applicability decision.

primary_questions.question: Does the case exhibit Shadow AI component usage: Unregistered or uncontrolled models, tools, providers, prompts or agent capabilities are used.
Do implemented workflows, data paths or operations show models selected directly in code, unofficial AI services, or tool sets that differ from architecture?
Does current evidence test presence or scoped absence of Shadow AI component usage, or does it remain unknown?

antipattern_indicators: No owner for a critical component

conditions: Refer verified shadow ai component usage to the accountable authority before progression where the condition materially affects the requested operating scope.

normative_source_mappings.relevant_locator: NIST AI 100-1, GOVERN 1.6 (PDF p. 28), MAP 4.2 (PDF p. 32), MANAGE 3.2 (PDF p. 37)
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: The voluntary framework provides guidance on maintaining AI inventory and monitoring dependencies and pre-trained models. The SAE criteria define the object-specific rules. Confirm any binding obligation through the accountable authority and its applicable source.

failure_mechanism: The declared or implemented control can be unreliable where architecture or inventory omits a component authorized or reachable at runtime. The mechanism can have an operational effect where run metadata shows an unofficial service, undeclared tool or unexpected model or prompt version.
potential_consequences: An unexplained decision may be impossible to tie to its actual component baseline.

atomic_tests.test: Compare the effective governance and design records. Determine whether architecture or inventory omits a component authorized or reachable at runtime. Identify the system scope and the record that supports each conclusion.

Trace actual configurations or activity for the assessed release. Determine whether run metadata shows an unofficial service, undeclared tool or unexpected model or prompt version. Attribute each observation to the specific path, time and decision.

Independently review comparison of inventory, released configuration and sampled normal and fallback run manifests. Record whether each material mechanism was tested, the observed result and the scope limitations.

required_evidence.title: Effective design and governance records
required_evidence.description: Review the versioned owner decision and relevant specifications for evidence of whether architecture or inventory omits a component authorized or reachable at runtime. Preserve material conflict and applicability context.

required_evidence.title: Observed condition or enforcement trace
required_evidence.description: Use effective configuration or dated operational records to determine whether run metadata shows an unofficial service, undeclared tool or unexpected model or prompt version. Identify the version, affected paths and period represented.

required_evidence.title: Executed scoped comparison
required_evidence.description: Provide comparison of inventory, released configuration and sampled normal and fallback run manifests. Include current scope, expected results, observed results, retained evidence and unresolved cases.

required_evidence.title: Independent review and limitations
required_evidence.description: An independent reviewer confirms the assessed version, completeness of coverage, result, limitations and whether a material change requires a new test.

required_artifacts: Comparison of inventory, released configuration and sampled normal and fallback run manifests.
Current version and scope with all material failure paths and cases identified.
Expected and observed results, attributable records, and independent review of coverage and residual limitations.

sufficiency: Presence requires affirmative evidence for a material mechanism. Examine whether architecture or inventory omits a component authorized or reachable at runtime, and separately check whether run metadata shows an unofficial service, undeclared tool or unexpected model or prompt version. A supported mechanism may establish presence within its evidenced scope.
Keep unresolved or contradictory mechanisms UNKNOWN and preserve the competing records. Refer material interpretation conflicts to the accountable human authority.

Use TESTED_ABSENT only after a current, executed, successful and independently verified evaluation covers all material paths within scope. Use comparison of inventory, released configuration and sampled normal and fallback run manifests. Reassess when material changes affect that scope.
evidence_rules.evidence_ceiling: A document can identify a declared gap. Effective configuration can demonstrate a reachable condition. Observed records support only their covered period and workflow. TESTED_ABSENT requires the complete scoped absence contract.
false_positive_guards: A provider model alias can be documented when the effective deployment identity and its limitations remain traceable.
Confirm that the observed or alleged condition applies to the current assessed release and a reachable path.
prohibited_inferences: A gap or UNKNOWN in C1 alone cannot establish AP-C1 presence.
Missing complaints, incident silence and unsuccessful collection cannot establish absence.
Model output and tactic selection grant no authority to approve, close a finding or accept risk.

finding_definitions.title: Design or intent shows shadow ai component usage
Implementation or operating evidence shows shadow ai component usage
Presence or tested absence of shadow ai component usage is unresolved within scope
